findings.note: redaction_test.go's fail-closed export guard has a hole that defeats its stated purpose. TestEverySnapshotFieldIsClassifiedForExport enumerates run.Snapshot with reflect.VisibleFields and then skips any field whose json tag is empty (redaction_test.go:82). An exported field added without a json tag is still marshalled by run.MarshalCanonical (internal/fsm/run/types.go:331, encoding/json) under its Go field name, so it would reach the evidence bundle unredacted while this test — the only structural enforcement, per its own header comment at redaction_test.go:10-20 — stays green. The empty-tag skip is needed only for unexported fields; the condition should be reflect.StructField.IsExported() rather than an empty tag, keeping the `-` skip. No live leak today (every Snapshot field is tagged), but the guard is future-proofing and this is the exact future it fails to cover.

findings.note: record_test.go leaks a package-level seam across tests. TestTornTailWritePath assigns nanos = func() int64 { return 42 } (record_test.go:160) and never restores it, while the neighbouring flock override in TestWriteErrors is carefully saved and restored (record_test.go:279-284). nanos names torn fragments (internal/fsm/record/record.go:223), so any later test in this package that produces two torn fragments in one .torn directory would have the second silently overwrite the first, and the failure would depend on test order. Benign today only because each later case uses a fresh t.TempDir. Fix: defer restoring nanos as flock does.

findings.note: The interleaved-writers regression test does not cover the branch where the race can still lose a row. TestRunsJSONLSurvivesInterleavedWriters (record_test.go:310) exercises only the plain-append path of appendRow, which is safe because of O_APPEND. The torn-tail repair branch (internal/fsm/record/record.go:218-226) still does readRows then f.Truncate(t.offset) while holding an advisory flock that state.AppendJSONL (internal/state/state.go:28-32) never takes, so an unlocked append landing in that window is truncated away. The test's own header comment asserts the two-writer invariant is now safe; that claim is untested for the repair path. Note the fix would land in record.go, which is outside this shard.

findings.note: TestK3Composition reuses one adjudicateOut variable across seven sub-cases and ignores every json.Unmarshal error (kind_test.go:356, 386, 403, 416, 472, 529). When a decode fails the previous case's field values survive into the next assertion, so a sub-case can pass on stale data. Today each sub-case is saved by the accompanying err != nil check or by differing expected shapes, so this is latent rather than active, but declaring `out` inside each block (or checking the unmarshal error) removes the class.
